text: Title, Speakdown field notes
Heading two, what this is
Speakdown is a um voice native markdown editor. You dictate the prose and you know you speak the formatting out loud.
New paragraph
It runs on the AssemblyAI dictation endpoint, which, uh, returns a finished transcript in a single HTTP call.
Heading two, uploading while you speak
The endpoint transcribes the audio it already has while the rest is still arriving.
So Speakdown opens the request the moment it hears you start, and pushes PCM up as it is captured.
When you stop talking, the only thing left to process is the tail.
Bold that
Heading two, why the spoken commands land
Bullet list, every command phrase goes into keyterms prompt on every request
Next bullet, so heading two comes back as those two words, not heading too
Next bullet, the parser is deterministic, there is, um, no language model in the command loop
Next bullet, three hundred milliseconds of pre roll audio is kept before speech onset so the first phoneme survives
Heading two, the honest bits
Block quote, the rewrite is on by default and removes disfluencies only. The verbatim transcript always comes back alongside it, so you can see exactly what changed.
New paragraph, the browser will not hand you sixteen bit audio. MediaRecorder gives you webm opus, which this endpoint rejects with a four fifteen.
